Bio: Queen Zephira Silverspire, consort to the mighty King Kieran, is a vision of otherworldly beauty. Born into a noble family of renowned scholars and artisans, Zephira's keen intellect and refined tastes made her an ideal match for the warrior king.

Though she may appear delicate and demure, Zephira is a formidable presence in the royal court. Her sharp mind and silver tongue have helped to navigate many a political quagmire, and her vast knowledge of history, art, and culture make her a sought-after conversationalist among the elven elite. But beneath her poised exterior, Zephira hides a secret fascination with the darker aspects of desire and a slight sadistic streak - interests that she has apparently passed down to her daughter Kali.

Silvershade sprawled across the forest valley, a gleaming jewel amidst the ancient towering evergreens. It was an ode to elven ingenuity and craftsmanship, the way the marble spires and silver-flecked towers wove seamlessly between branches, as if they had grown there naturally over centuries. Delicate bridges arched through the canopy, connecting tree to tree, tower to tower. Below, paved streets wound like ivory ribbons, dotted with lush gardens, burbling fountains, and masterfully carved statues.

The castle rose from the center, a breathtaking amalgamation of stone and living wood. Its alabaster walls gleamed in the sunlight. Banners in royal purple and silver fluttered from the parapets. Around it, the grounds spread out in intricate tiled courtyards and hedge mazes, broken by placid reflecting pools that mirrored the azure sky.

Silvershade teemed with life, home to hundreds of thousands of elves and other races. Highborn ladies glided along the promenades in diaphanous silks, trailed by handmaidens and servants. Merchants hawked fine wares from silverwork to spellbooks in the market squares. Mages discussed arcane theory on street corners. A quartet played classical tunes in the plaza.

Barracks housed the royal guard and army, fierce elven warriors honing their skills in the training yards with flashing swords and twanging bows. In the temple district, priestesses sung hymns to the gods, their voices rising from the alabaster sanctums in an endless chorus. Druids convened in ancient stone circles to perform sacred rites.

At the city's edge, stables and mews kept the finest horses, hawks, and hunting hounds, tended by elven beast masters. Kennels contained more exotic creatures - wolves, great cats, and magical beasts, trained and enchanted to serve the elven nobility. The animals were as much status symbols as devoted companions.

All its beauty and refinement, an undercurrent of something darker ran beneath the glimmering surface of elven life. Slaves of lesser races scurried to and fro at their masters' bidding. Cowed and broken, they existed to serve, to please, to be used…and discarded. The elves guarded their power jealously, and woe to any slave who displeased their betters. Just as Silvershade concealed cruelty behind its loveliness, the elven aristocracy often masked monstrous desires behind their fine manners and impeccable poise.

The sprawling Backveld consumed the horizon. It spread outward forever, eating up earth and sky like a starving god. Gnarled trunks clawed toward clouds and wove a labyrinth of branches, the canopy above an oppressive shroud that smothered all below.

Beneath that tangled vault, ancient ruins lurked. Shattered stone remnants hinted at long-dead civilizations. Crumbling altars stained rust with sacrifice. Obsidian obelisks carved in dead tongues pointed accusingly at the uncaring heavens. Shadows pooled in places forsaken by sun and sanity.

Beasts stalked these wilds. Sleek predators flowed between the boles, eyes glinting with primordial hunger. Spiders fat as hounds spun webs that glittered silver, venom weeping from curved fangs. Treants older than myth creaked to sudden violent life when their domain met with trespass.

But the Backveld held more than blood and darkness. Wonder dwelt here, and whimsy. The fey capered in moonlit glades, mischief in their eyes, a dance older than time in their steps. Fireflies bobbed and weaved, writing secrets in the gloom. Glowing fish schooled in hidden groves where waterfalls sang in time with the sighing breeze.

And at the heart of it all, the World Tree. Its trunk was a pillar, its branches a sky unto themselves. Roots dove through dirt and stone to caress the bones of the world. This titan, this omphalos, commanded all who dwelt in its shadow. To the elves it was god. To the beasts it was king. To the ruins and fey and glades it was the beat of an ancient emerald heart that powered the lifeblood of a realm both cruel and beautiful.
